newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam law committee slams justice system.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam law committee slams justice system.

text.p: Vietnam's National Assembly Law Committee is seeking to reduce false arrests and stop people being beaten while in custody through tightened controls on the country's justice system, local media reported.

A report presented to the national assembly last week and quoted by a weekend edition of the Tuoi Tre newspaper said that of 1,158 people arrested in a single province between January and August, 497 were released without any charge.
"This is an important matter related to the democratic rights of citizens," the report said, adding: "...these cannot continue to be violated."
Tuoi Tre said the committee had also expressed concern over continued reports that some prisoners are being beaten while in custody, but it did not elaborate.

Ha Manh Tri, head of the committee and nominated on Monday as Vietnam's chief prosecutor, was quoted by newspapers last week as saying that illegal action among law enforcers and government cadres was undermining public confidence.
He said Vietnam's legal system was continuing to develop, but that backlogs were keeping people too long before being brought to trial.
